data.body:
Fixes bug Bfc4ac64c9c: DX-agent-final-summary landed on main (e1574c74, merge gate passed) but a crash left it ABANDONED with a worktree holding 2 stale pin/merge commits. 'ddflow cleanup' lists it 'unmerged ... Finish it, or merge deliberately' with 0 safe actions, though the item's merge gate is done and the report says landed. Cleanup should recognise landed-on-main items with only pin/merge leftovers and offer removal; I removed worktree+branch by hand (leftover content stale vs main). Found on DX-agent-final-summary.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bfc4ac64c9c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bfc4ac64c9c --regression-test <test>` first).

chunk_findings.detail:
The marker is now written before `_guarded`, but the early-return path
`if isinstance(done, O.Outcome): return done` does not call
`RUN.clear_started(marker)`. For any run where `_guarded` produces an
`O.Outcome` (the same function is used as a pre-execution guard whose
declined path is explicitly handled by this line), the new
`{gate}.running.{pid}.json` marker is left behind while the current process is
still alive. A second process starting the same gate on the same commit before
the first process exits therefore sees this marker as a live twin and is
refused, naming a process that never started the gate execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:646-672 (`run`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new mark-then-check sequence is still non-atomic: `mark_started` snapshots `clock.now_iso()` into `m.at` before its marker file is made visible. Interleaving: process A computes `at=...000` and is then descheduled before writing; process B computes `at=...001`, writes its marker, calls `live_run` (A's file is absent) and proceeds; A resumes, writes its marker, sees B, and because `(B.at, B.pid) > (A.at, A.pid)` is true, A also proceeds. Both run the same gate on the same commit, violating exactly-one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:_mark_or_refuse_twin, ddflow/services/gates/running.py:mark_started

chunk_findings.detail: The marker is now written before `_guarded`, but it is only cleared on the normal `_execute` path via `marker = run.pop("marker")`. If `_guarded` returns an `O.Outcome` (the branch `if isinstance(done, O.Outcome): return done`), the marker is never passed to `RUN.clear_started`. While the host process remains alive, a subsequent same-commit run sees this leaked marker as a live twin and is refused even though the first invocation never executed the gate. The marker must be cleared before every early return after `mark_started`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: `_reap` unconditionally runs `os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)`. When the process has already exited (for example, the second `ddflow gate run` is wrongly refused and exits before the `finally` block), its session/process group is gone, so `killpg` raises `ProcessLookupError`. In `test_a_run_on_a_newer_commit_is_allowed_while_the_first_lives`, this overrides the actual assertion failure and also prevents cleanup. A simple `p.poll() is None` guard before `killpg` would avoid this, but as written the test can fail for the wrong reason.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_same_commit_live.py:_reap

chunk_findings.detail: The marker is now created by `_mark_or_refuse_twin` before `_guarded`, but the branch `if isinstance(done, O.Outcome): return done` returns before `marker = run.pop("marker")` and before the `try/finally` that calls `RUN.clear_started(marker)`. If `_guarded` returns an `O.Outcome` for a declined/pre-execution guard (rather than the run dictionary that is later executed), the new `{gate}.running.{pid}.json` marker is never cleared while the calling process remains alive. Concrete failure: process A calls `gate.run` for commit C and `_guarded` declines, returning `O.Outcome`; A continues running as a live daemon. Process B then starts the same gate on C; `RUN.live_run` sees A's stale marker with a live pid and refuses B with “already running”, even though A is not executing the gate. The author's triage probe at lines 695-722 is the later allowed-run try/finally in `run`, not a clear inside `_guarded`, so it does not answer this branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:650-672

chunk_findings.detail: `start_lock` opens a lock file at `_dir(repo, item) / f"{gate}.lock"` but does not ensure `_dir(repo, item)` exists. On the first run ever for an item, that directory is absent, so `fsio.file_lock` raises `FileNotFoundError` (an `OSError`); the handler yields with no lock held. Two processes starting the same gate on the same commit at the same time for a new item can both take this unlocked path. `live_run` then returns `None` while `d.is_dir()` is still false, before any marker exists, so both can write their own markers and proceed; even in the mark-then-check ordering the docstring assumes, both can mark before either scans and both can then see the other as a live twin. The guarantee “of two runs started together exactly one sees the other’s marker” does not hold exactly when the first twin starts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/running.py start_lock

evidence.budget_forced: round 3: code changed after round 2 (flock replaces timestamp tie-break) to fix its confirmed finding

chunk_findings.detail: `start_lock` still does not make mark-then-check atomic in the fallback path: `except (OSError, fsio.LockTimeout): yield return`. Concrete interleaving: process A acquires the lock, `mark_started` computes `m.at`, and A is SIGSTOPed before the marker file is written. Process B waits `timeout_s=30`, catches `fsio.LockTimeout`, and yields unlocked. B writes its marker, sees no A marker, and proceeds. When A resumes, it writes its marker, sees B, and—by the `(B.at,B.pid) > (A.at,A.pid)` logic from finding 1—A also proceeds. Both run the same gate on the same commit, exactly the violation finding 1 described. The new test only exercises the lock-acquired path, so it does not answer this still-live lock-failure path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/running.py:start_lock

chunk_findings.detail: The author's triage says `_guarded` wraps every return in `try/finally RUN.clear_started(marker)`. When `_guarded` returns the normal run dictionary that is later executed, that `finally` runs before control returns to `run`, so the just-created started marker is deleted. `run` then pops the already-cleared marker at line 692 and executes `_execute` without any live marker. Concrete failure: process A starts a long-running gate; once `_guarded` returns and A enters `_execute`, its marker file is gone; process B starts the same gate on the same commit and `_mark_or_refuse_twin` sees no live twin, so B is allowed, defeating the same-commit refusal exactly during execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:_guarded with ddflow/api/gates.py:692

chunk_findings.detail: When `proc_start` cannot be verified for a marker — either because `m.pid_start` is empty or because `proc_start(m.pid)` returns `""` — the expression `m.pid_start and now and now != m.pid_start` is false, so `not (...)` is true and `_is_live` degrades to `alive(m.pid)` alone. A stale marker whose original PID has since been reused by a different live process is then treated as the original run, so a new same-commit run is refused naming an unrelated recycled PID. The unverifiable-start-time case should be treated as not-live, not live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/running.py:_is_live

chunk_findings.detail: `test_start_lock_serialises_mark_and_look` does not prove the second thread has reached `RUN.start_lock(...).__enter__()` before `release.set()`. After `t2.join(0.5)`, `assert order == ["a-in"]` succeeds both when `t2` is correctly blocked on the lock and when `t2` has not been scheduled yet. If `start_lock` were broken and did not serialize, but the OS delayed `t2` until after `release.set()` and `"a-out"`, the final order would still be `["a-in", "a-out", "b-in"]`, so the test could pass for a non-serializing `start_lock`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_same_commit_live.py:137-142

evidence.budget_forced: round 4: lock timeout fallback removed to fix round 3's confirmed finding; tree changed since

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test does not exercise the previously confirmed HIGH interleaving. The old bug only appeared after `timeout_s=30`, when `fsio.LockTimeout` was caught and the context yielded unlocked. This test waits only 0.5s for the second `start_lock.__enter__` to block and then releases the lock before 30s, so an implementation with that exact fallback would still see `order == ["a-in"]` at 0.5s and would pass. It also never calls `mark_started`/`live_run` inside the lock, so it does not verify that the actual `gate run` path keeps mark-then-check inside the critical section.

chunk_findings.detail: `_mark_or_refuse_twin` now creates a started marker before the existing `_guarded` guard runs. If `_guarded` returns an `O.Outcome` (the very next `if isinstance(done, O.Outcome): return done` path), this code returns immediately without calling `RUN.clear_started` or entering `RUN.terminating()`. For example, a no-op or otherwise guard-refused `run` in a long-lived process leaves the current PID’s marker behind; a later `run` on the same commit then has `RUN.live_run` see that still-live PID and is refused even though no gate is executing. Previously `RUN.mark_started` happened after this early return, so guard refusals did not leave a marker.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:649

chunk_findings.detail: The lock path is `_dir(repo, item) / f"{gate}.lock"`, but `start_lock` does not ensure `_dir(repo, item)` exists. On a fresh repo/item, `.ddflow/runs/<item>` does not exist yet; `fsio.file_lock(...)` cannot open a file in a missing directory and raises `FileNotFoundError`, which is caught by `except OSError`, so the context yields unlocked. Two simultaneous first runs of the same item/gate/sha are therefore not serialized: both can call `mark_started` and then `live_run`; once both markers exist, each sees the other's live marker and both refuse. That fails the “exactly one sees the other's marker” guarantee in the only initial-contention case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/running.py:start_lock

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test still does not exercise the previously confirmed buggy interleaving. The old bug only appears when the lock acquisition times out after `timeout_s=30` and the `fsio.LockTimeout` path yields unlocked; this test sleeps only 1.5 s, asserts the second thread has not entered, and then releases the first lock well before that timeout. A `start_lock` implementation with the exact bug still reports `order == ["a-in"]` at line 141 and still ends with `["a-in", "a-out", "b-in"]`, so it would pass. The change from 0.5 s to 1.5 s does not reach the 30 s fallback, and the test still never runs `mark_started`/`live_run` inside the held lock to observe the unlocked second entry.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_same_commit_live.py:141
